The same in every edition') a SYNCHRONIZED LEFT item cannot be placed so as to falsify GR3; my probe s13lr.cob (run s13lr-002) measured binary items of 2, 4 and 8 bytes under SYNC, SYNC LEFT and SYNC RIGHT in WORKING-STORAGE groups, under OCCURS, a signed DISPLAY item, a level-77 item and a file record written and read back: every item begins at the byte after its predecessor and the record is 15 bytes (no slack; USAGE INDEX with SYNC is refused at 85 by the binder, DataBinder.SynchronizedViolation). The layout code never reads DataItem.Synchronized. So the closed set (no natural boundary wider than one character) is TRUE. But the ARM does not fit. indistinguishable-consequent needs GR3's consequent to be the SAME as GR1's for every program both admit. It is not: under one-character boundaries GR3 is satisfied by EVERY placement (even one that overlaps another item onto the SYNC item), while GR1 ('no other data item occupies any of the character positions between the leftmost and rightmost natural boundaries delimiting this data item') is falsified by an overlap. GR1's own 1985 golden says so in its header: conformance-suite/cases/VI.5.13@1985-SYNCHRONIZED-CLAUSE/g85_f09_02.cob, 'GR3 (LEFT) and GR4 (RIGHT) are NOT claimed: with every position a natural boundary they hold for every placement, so no leg here can fail for a GR3 or GR4 reason', while its L-* legs CAN fail for a GR1 reason. A compiler that overlays the item's neighbour fails GR1 and passes GR3: the two rules are distinguishable, and the argument's own sentence 'a compiler that honours GR1 cannot fail GR3' is an implication, not sameness (a compiler that breaks GR1 cannot fail GR3 either). Also the argument's 'it begins at the byte after the preceding item, with no slack ... is GR1' over-reads GR1: slack BEFORE the item lies outside its boundaries and neither GR1 nor GR3 forbids it; that fact is the A.1 item 197 determination's alone. No arm of DESIGN-spec-conformance-review section 1.1 states the true case (the consequent holds in every reachable state because the implementor's boundary makes every placement satisfy it): not unpopulatable-antecedent (the antecedent, SYNC LEFT written, is reachable), not this arm, not definitional (the subject is the implementation's positioning), not undefined-in-rule. Note the 2023 twin GR-13.18.55.4-4 is closed CONFORMS by a layout test (l1_byte_length_implicit_filler, pb538-sync-left-right-differ) that pins the same determination, which g85_f09_02 refuses to claim for 1985: the two editions treat the same fact two ways.

The repository reads the twin sentence the same way: SequentialConnector's remarks ground the '39' for a keyed store on 'The file organization is established at the time a physical file is created and cannot subsequently be changed' as an obligation on the runtime. A program OBSERVES the first half without breaking the second: g18rd2.cob creates a report file under RECORD CONTAINS 20 CHARACTERS (a fixed-length file, II.2.1.4.1) and reads it back through a second SELECT of the same file with the SAME 20-character description, so no program changed the sizes. Observed: READ 00 [ROW 1            END], READ 00 [CRLF + 'ROW 2            E'], READ 04, READ 10: the file the implementation created holds 22-byte line records, not the 20-character records established at its creation. With the line not filled to its width (g18rd.cob) the records are cut to 5 characters, which also contradicts docs/conformance DOC-A.1-159 ('the record is the size the FD's RECORD clause gives it: integer-1 bytes in Format 1'). The second half (no later program may change the sizes) is a constraint on the user's programs; the first half is not, so the row cannot stand on definitional.
